name: Circle Loop
statusNote: Researched and trained before the arena rules existed. The run uses the historical matrix-cost accounting at +4.2% against SSSL under the same accounting, candidates were judged on periodic validation BPB and subset CORE, and no checkpoint is published.

people.name: NextTransformer contributors
people.role: Proposed the ring design, made the design decisions, launched and monitored the runs

llms.name: ChatGPT
llms.role: Novelty assessment against prior looped models and the first formalization of per-block halting

llms.name: Codex
llms.role: Implementation plans, halter, budget controller, loss and curriculum, code, tests, cost estimates, launch commands, and failure diagnosis

framework.name: none
framework.note: Interactive ChatGPT and Codex desktop sessions; no auto-research framework

researcher.involvementNote: The idea came from a person, who also kept Circle as the main line, pointed out that exited tokens were still computed, and set the 3 + 9 + 3 layout. The agents designed the halter, budget control, loss, and curriculum and did all implementation.

research.formalNote: Two launches exited before training (mount path, reused output directory); one stopped at update 430 on a storage-quota error without a checkpoint; the fourth launch completed.
research.computeNote: Not metered. Candidates: GPT-2-backbone Circle-ST (stopped when the study moved to the d24 shell), a 2 + 8 + 2 d24 version (about 8,000 updates), and the final 3 + 9 + 3 design after a 128-update pilot. The formal run took under four and a half days on one 8-GPU node.

novelty.statement: Ring reuse and token-adaptive depth exist already. Circle Loop exits per block inside a ring of nine distinct shared blocks: after one full circuit, a shared halter that reads only a token's current state and its change, with no depth input, decides after every block whether the token continues; exited states freeze and leave later ring attention, and a maximum-entropy depth target with a dual controller holds the mean ring depth at 17.5.
